group.passage:
Next time you cross a street, look down at the corner of the sidewalk. Chances are you will find a gentle ramp, known as a curb cut, [[1]] a sharp step. For a person in a wheelchair, even a low curb [[2]] a wall, which is why disability activists in the United States pushed cities in the 1970s to cut ramps into their street corners.
Cities were slow to act, but the ramps gradually spread, and what happened next surprised many people. Parents pushing strollers, travelers pulling suitcases, and delivery workers with heavy carts soon discovered that the ramps [[3]] them a great deal of effort. A change made for a small group had quietly made the street better for nearly everyone, a pattern now known as the curb-cut effect.
The same thing has happened again and again. Captions, first created for viewers who are deaf, are now [[4]] by people watching videos on noisy trains or learning a new language. Recorded books, long produced for blind readers, now keep many drivers company on long trips. Designing for people at the [[5]], it seems, often improves life for those in the middle, too.

tags.key_phrase: might as well be（簡直就是、和……沒兩樣）
save someone effort（省去某人的力氣）
people at the edges（處在邊緣的人）

1.explanation_zh: in place of 是「取代、代替」。人行道轉角原本是一個陡直的台階，現在換成一個平緩的斜坡，也就是「路緣斜坡」：用斜坡取代了台階。
evidence: Chances are you will find a gentle ramp, known as a curb cut, [[1]] a sharp step.

option_notes_zh.A: 【強誘答・CN】in charge of（負責、掌管）和正解同樣是「in＋名詞＋of」，但斜坡不會「負責」台階。
option_notes_zh.C: in favor of 是「贊成、偏好」，通常用來說人支持某一方；斜坡不會「贊成」台階。
option_notes_zh.D: in need of 是「需要」，「平緩的斜坡需要一個陡直的台階」不合邏輯。

1.strategy_zh: gentle ramp（平緩的斜坡）和 sharp step（陡直的台階）是一組對比，空格要表示兩者的關係：用前者取代後者。四個選項都是「in＋名詞＋of」，要分辨中間的名詞。線索在本句。
hints: gentle ramp 和 sharp step 是相似還是相反的東西？
路緣斜坡和原本的台階是什麼關係？

2.explanation_zh: might as well be 是「簡直就是、和……沒兩樣」。對坐輪椅的人來說，即使是很矮的路緣，也像一堵牆一樣過不去，這正是（which is why）身障運動人士要推動各城市在街角切出斜坡的原因。
evidence: For a person in a wheelchair, even a low curb [[2]] a wall, which is why disability activists in the United States pushed cities in the 1970s to cut ramps into their street corners.

option_notes_zh.B: 【強誘答・GN】may well have been 也有 may、well、be，看起來很像；但它是對過去的推測「很可能曾經是」，本句說的是一個一直存在的情況（對輪椅使用者而言路緣就像牆），不是在推測過去。
option_notes_zh.C: had better be 是「最好是」，表示建議或警告，「矮路緣最好是一堵牆」不通。
option_notes_zh.D: would rather be 是「寧願是」，主詞要是有意願的人，路緣不會「寧願」成為一堵牆。

2.strategy_zh: even a low curb（即使是很矮的路緣）提示「就算很矮，對輪椅使用者來說也等於……」；後半句 which is why 也說明這正是要切斜坡的原因。四個選項都是情態助動詞的慣用結構，要分辨「簡直就是」「很可能曾經是」「最好是」「寧願是」。線索在本句。
hints: 對坐輪椅的人來說，就算路緣很矮，也像什麼一樣難以通過？
which is why 說這就是什麼事的原因？
要選表示「簡直就是、和……沒兩樣」的結構。

3.explanation_zh: save someone something 是「省去某人……」。推嬰兒車的父母、拉行李箱的旅客、推著沉重推車的送貨員都發現，斜坡替他們省下很多力氣；下一句也說，這個為少數人所做的改變，讓街道對幾乎每個人都變得更好。
evidence: Parents pushing strollers, travelers pulling suitcases, and delivery workers with heavy carts soon discovered that the ramps [[3]] them a great deal of effort.
A change made for a small group had quietly made the street better for nearly everyone

option_notes_zh.A: 【強誘答・LR】cost them a great deal of effort（讓他們費很多力氣）文法完全正確，cost 也常接雙受詞；但下一句說這個改變讓街道對幾乎每個人都更好，方向相反。
option_notes_zh.B: clear 不能這樣接雙受詞，「清除他們很多力氣」語意不通。
option_notes_zh.C: earn 接雙受詞時是「為某人贏得（好處、名聲）」，「為他們贏得很多力氣」不通。

3.strategy_zh: 四個動詞後面都接 them＋a great deal of effort，要判斷斜坡對這些推著重物的人是「省力」還是「費力」。第一段的 gentle ramp 與下一句的 made the street better for nearly everyone 都指向省力。線索在下一句與第一段。
hints: 推嬰兒車、拉行李箱的人，走斜坡比上下台階輕鬆還是辛苦？
下一句說這個改變對幾乎所有人的影響是好是壞？
要選表示「省去某人力氣」的動詞。

4.explanation_zh: switch on 是「打開（開關）」。字幕原本是為聽障觀眾設計的，現在在吵雜火車上看影片的人（聽不清楚聲音），或在學新語言的人（需要對照文字），也會把字幕打開，這正是路緣斜坡效應的又一個例子。
evidence: The same thing has happened again and again.
Captions, first created for viewers who are deaf, are now [[4]] by people watching videos on noisy trains or learning a new language.

option_notes_zh.A: 【強誘答・LR】switched off 和正解只差一個介副詞；但在吵雜的火車上聽不清楚聲音，學語言也需要看文字，這些人是要「打開」字幕，關掉字幕就不是「同樣的事又發生了」。
option_notes_zh.B: shut down 是「關閉（工廠、系統）」，用在字幕上不自然，方向也和情境相反。
option_notes_zh.D: left out 是「省略、遺漏」，「字幕被這些人省略掉」與他們需要字幕的情境相反。

4.strategy_zh: The same thing has happened again and again 表示本句是另一個「為少數人設計、結果大家都受惠」的例子。再看情境：noisy trains、learning a new language，這些人需要字幕。線索在本句與前一句。
hints: The same thing 指的是哪一種現象？
在吵雜的火車上看影片，會想打開還是關掉字幕？

5.explanation_zh: people at the edges 指「處在邊緣的人」，也就是人數少、常被忽略的群體，例如本文提到的輪椅使用者、聽障者和盲人。為這些人設計的東西（路緣斜坡、字幕、有聲書），結果也讓處在「中間」的一般大眾生活得更好。
evidence: A change made for a small group had quietly made the street better for nearly everyone
Designing for people at the [[5]], it seems, often improves life for those in the middle, too.

option_notes_zh.A: 【強誘答・LR】center（中心）和句尾的 middle 意思相近，看起來互相呼應；但本句是用「為某些人設計」對比「連中間的一般人也受惠」，為中心的人設計就沒有對比，也不符合全文「為少數人設計」的主旨。
option_notes_zh.B: people at the top 指「社會頂層、位高權重的人」，全文談的是輪椅使用者和聽障、視障者，不是有權勢的人。
option_notes_zh.C: people at the front 是「排在前面的人」，與全文談的身障者無關。

5.strategy_zh: 本句是全文的結論：為 ___ 的人設計，也讓 those in the middle（中間的人）受惠，前後是一組對比。回想全文：斜坡、字幕、有聲書原本都是為少數身障者設計的，也就是處在「邊緣」的人。線索在第二段的 a small group 與全文（距離超過兩句）。
hints: 全文的例子原本是為哪些人設計的？他們是多數還是少數？
句尾的 those in the middle 和空格是相同還是相對的位置？

translation_zh.text:
下次過馬路時，低頭看看人行道的轉角。你很可能會看到一個平緩的斜坡取代了陡直的台階，這叫做「路緣斜坡」。對坐輪椅的人來說，即使是很矮的路緣也簡直就是一堵牆，這正是為什麼 1970 年代美國的身障運動人士要推動各城市在街角切出斜坡。
各城市行動得很慢，但斜坡逐漸普及，接下來發生的事讓許多人感到意外。推著嬰兒車的父母、拉著行李箱的旅客，以及推著沉重推車的送貨員很快就發現，斜坡替他們省下了很多力氣。一項為少數人所做的改變，悄悄讓街道對幾乎每個人都變得更好，這種模式現在被稱為「路緣斜坡效應」。
同樣的事一再發生。字幕最初是為聽障觀眾設計的，如今在吵雜的火車上看影片的人，或是正在學新語言的人，也會把字幕打開。長久以來為盲人讀者製作的有聲書，現在陪伴許多駕駛度過漫長的車程。看來，為處在邊緣的人設計，往往也能讓處在中間的人生活得更好。

evidence: Chances are you will find a gentle ramp, known as a curb cut, [[1]] a sharp step.
1.explanation_zh: 人行道轉角是緩坡「取代」陡階，in place of 正確；in charge of 負責、in favor of 贊成、in need of 需要，皆不合。

evidence: For a person in a wheelchair, even a low curb [[2]] a wall, which is why disability activists in the United States pushed cities in the 1970s to cut ramps into their street corners.
2.explanation_zh: 對坐輪椅者而言，即使低矮的路緣「簡直就像」一道牆，might as well be 表「跟……沒兩樣」，且是現在式泛論；may well have been 是對過去的推測，時態不合；had better be、would rather be 表建議、偏好，主詞是物不通。

evidence: Parents pushing strollers, travelers pulling suitcases, and delivery workers with heavy carts soon discovered that the ramps [[3]] them a great deal of effort.
A change made for a small group had quietly made the street better for nearly everyone, a pattern now known as the curb-cut effect.
3.explanation_zh: 推嬰兒車、拉行李的人發現坡道「替他們省了」很多力氣，save sb. effort 正確，下句也說讓街道對幾乎每個人都更好；cost them effort 文法可行但意思相反；cleared、earned 不與 effort 這樣搭配。

evidence: Captions, first created for viewers who are deaf, are now [[4]] by people watching videos on noisy trains or learning a new language.
4.explanation_zh: 字幕原本為聽障者設計，現在也被在吵雜車廂看影片或學外語的人「打開使用」，switched on 正確；switched off、shut down 關掉，left out 遺漏，都與「其他人也受益」的文意相反。

evidence: Designing for people at the [[5]], it seems, often improves life for those in the middle, too.
5.explanation_zh: 與 those in the middle 對比，指為「邊緣」（少數、特殊需求）的人設計，at the edges 正確；center 與 middle 同義無對比，top、front 也不與 middle 形成「邊緣 vs 中間」的對照。

evidence: Chances are you will find a gentle ramp, known as a curb cut, [[1]] a sharp step.
1.explanation_zh: 斜坡「取代」了陡峭的台階，in place of a sharp step；in favor of 或 in need of 語意不合。

evidence: For a person in a wheelchair, even a low curb [[2]] a wall, which is why disability activists in the United States pushed cities in the 1970s to cut ramps into their street corners.
2.explanation_zh: 對輪椅使用者而言，連低矮的路緣也「簡直就像一堵牆」，might as well be 是現在式的比喻說法，後面也說活動人士因此爭取斜坡。

evidence: Parents pushing strollers, travelers pulling suitcases, and delivery workers with heavy carts soon discovered that the ramps [[3]] them a great deal of effort.
3.explanation_zh: 推嬰兒車、拉行李箱的人發現斜坡「幫他們省了」許多力氣，save somebody effort。

evidence: Captions, first created for viewers who are deaf, are now [[4]] by people watching videos on noisy trains or learning a new language.
4.explanation_zh: 字幕本來為聽障者設計，現在在嘈雜火車上看影片的人也會「開啟」使用，switched on 符合語意。

evidence: Designing for people at the [[5]], it seems, often improves life for those in the middle, too.
5.explanation_zh: 針對邊緣（edges）的族群設計，也改善了中間族群的生活，與 those in the middle 呼應。

A.evidence: Chances are you will find a gentle ramp, known as a curb cut, [[1]] a sharp step.
A.explanation_zh: in charge of（負責、掌管）：斜坡不會「負責」台階。

C.evidence: Chances are you will find a gentle ramp, known as a curb cut, [[1]] a sharp step.
C.explanation_zh: X in favor of Y 是「捨 X 而取 Y」，用在這裡變成選了台階、捨棄斜坡，方向相反；作「贊成」解也不通，斜坡不會贊成台階。

D.evidence: Chances are you will find a gentle ramp, known as a curb cut, [[1]] a sharp step.
D.explanation_zh: in need of（需要）：「平緩的斜坡需要一個陡直的台階」不合邏輯；gentle ramp 與 sharp step 是取代關係。

B.evidence: For a person in a wheelchair, even a low curb [[2]] a wall, which is why disability activists in the United States pushed cities in the 1970s to cut ramps into their street corners.
B.explanation_zh: may well have been 是對過去的推測「很可能曾經就是」，把「矮路緣對輪椅使用者簡直就是一堵牆」的比喻變成字面推測；本句是現在式的一般陳述。

C.evidence: For a person in a wheelchair, even a low curb [[2]] a wall, which is why disability activists in the United States pushed cities in the 1970s to cut ramps into their street corners.
C.explanation_zh: had better be（最好是）表建議或警告，「矮路緣最好是一堵牆」不通。

D.evidence: For a person in a wheelchair, even a low curb [[2]] a wall, which is why disability activists in the United States pushed cities in the 1970s to cut ramps into their street corners.
D.explanation_zh: would rather be（寧願是）的主詞要是有意願的人，路緣不會「寧願」是一堵牆。

A.evidence: A change made for a small group had quietly made the street better for nearly everyone, a pattern now known as the curb-cut effect.
A.explanation_zh: cost them a great deal of effort 文法正確，但下一句說這個改變讓街道對幾乎每個人都更好，「斜坡讓他們費很多力」方向相反。

B.evidence: Parents pushing strollers, travelers pulling suitcases, and delivery workers with heavy carts soon discovered that the ramps [[3]] them a great deal of effort.
B.explanation_zh: clear 不能以「人＋effort」接雙受詞，「清除他們很多力氣」語意不通。

C.evidence: Parents pushing strollers, travelers pulling suitcases, and delivery workers with heavy carts soon discovered that the ramps [[3]] them a great deal of effort.
C.explanation_zh: earn 接雙受詞是「為某人贏得（好處、名聲）」，「為他們贏得很多力氣」不通。

A.evidence: The same thing has happened again and again.
A.explanation_zh: 本句是「為少數人設計、結果大家受惠」的另一個例子；在吵雜火車上聽不清楚、學語言要對照文字的人需要字幕，關掉字幕就不是「同樣的事」。

B.evidence: Captions, first created for viewers who are deaf, are now [[4]] by people watching videos on noisy trains or learning a new language.
B.explanation_zh: shut down 用於工廠、系統的關閉，用在字幕上不自然，方向也和情境相反。

D.evidence: Captions, first created for viewers who are deaf, are now [[4]] by people watching videos on noisy trains or learning a new language.
D.explanation_zh: leave out 是「省略、遺漏」，「字幕被這些人省略」與他們需要字幕的情境相反。

A.evidence: Designing for people at the [[5]], it seems, often improves life for those in the middle, too.
A.explanation_zh: center 和句尾的 the middle 同義，前後就失去對比；全文說的是為少數人設計、大家受惠。

B.evidence: For a person in a wheelchair, even a low curb [[2]] a wall, which is why disability activists in the United States pushed cities in the 1970s to cut ramps into their street corners.
B.explanation_zh: 全文的例子是坐輪椅的人、聽障觀眾、盲人讀者，是處在邊緣、人數少的群體，不是 people at the top（社會頂層、有權勢的人）。

C.evidence: Designing for people at the [[5]], it seems, often improves life for those in the middle, too.
C.explanation_zh: people at the front（排在前面的人）和身障者無關，也無法和 those in the middle 形成「邊緣—中間」的對照。
